sources.title: The Five Forces
sources.author: Harvard Business School Institute for Strategy and Competitiveness; Michael Porter framework
sources.reliability: high for framework definition; not independent outcome evidence
sources.notes: Page identifies original Porter 1979 article; page publication year is not supplied.
sources.access_evidence: Web page retrieved with full five forces descriptions and dynamic industry structure section.
supported_claims: Five forces concern rivalry, entry, substitutes, buyers and suppliers.
Industry structure affects profitability and evolves over time.
Substitutes satisfy the same underlying need differently.

sources.title: The Value Chain
sources.author: Harvard Business School Institute for Strategy and Competitiveness; Michael Porter framework
sources.reliability: high for definition; not outcome evidence
sources.access_evidence: Retrieved introduction and activities, competitive advantage and set of choices sections.
supported_claims: Activities and their configuration are units of competitive advantage.
Chain focuses on activities leading to higher prices or lower costs.
Company chain belongs to a wider supplier and distribution value system.

sources.title: SWOT analysis
sources.author: CIPD
sources.reliability: high for professional exposition; not origin attribution or outcome evidence
sources.notes: Factsheet dated 20 May 2026; no unverified single-inventor claim.
supported_claims: Strengths and weaknesses are internal; opportunities and threats are external.
Process proceeds from information gathering to important issues, options and priorities.

sources.title: PESTLE analysis
sources.author: CIPD; updated by David Hayden
sources.reliability: high for professional exposition; not legal advice or outcome evidence
sources.access_evidence: Six categories, workflow, tips and disadvantages retrieved.
supported_claims: Six categories are political, economic, sociological, technological, legal and environmental.
Scope should reflect industry and regions; regular monitoring is needed.
Insufficient or excessive data and unfounded assumptions limit analysis.

sources.title: What Is the Growth Share Matrix?
sources.author: Boston Consulting Group
sources.reliability: high for original framework logic; historical assumptions need local validation
sources.notes: 1970 is framework popularization year, not this page publication date.
sources.access_evidence: Retrieved full overview and how matrix works section.
supported_claims: Axes use relative market share and market growth.
Categories are stars, cash cows, question marks and pets.
Original model links market leadership with cost advantage.

sources.title: Enduring Ideas: The GE–McKinsey nine-box matrix
sources.author: McKinsey & Company; Kevin Coyne presentation
sources.reliability: high for framework exposition; not a validated investment algorithm
sources.access_evidence: Two factors and interpretation above, on and below diagonal retrieved.
supported_claims: Portfolio allocation uses industry attractiveness and competitive strength.
Matrix suggests investment, selective investment or cash/divestment discussions.
Categorization is a starting point; judgment remains necessary.

sources.title: Four Actions Framework
sources.author: W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne / Blue Ocean Strategy
sources.reliability: high for definition; authors site is not independent outcome evidence
sources.access_evidence: Authors official tool page retrieved: four questions and ERRC relationship.
supported_claims: Actions are eliminate, reduce, raise and create.
They reconstruct buyer value while pursuing differentiation and low cost.
All four questions should be considered together.

sources.title: Shell Scenarios
sources.author: Shell
sources.reliability: high for Shell practice description; not endorsement of substantive forecasts
sources.notes: Page contains 2026 scenarios; no web publication year inferred.
sources.access_evidence: Overview and formal cautionary note retrieved.
supported_claims: Scenarios explore possible futures and challenge assumptions for present decisions.
They are not predictions or company strategy.
Exploratory scenarios differ from normative scenarios with a stipulated outcome.

sources.title: On becoming a strategic partner: The role of human resources in gaining competitive advantage
sources.author: Jay B. Barney and Patrick M. Wright
sources.reliability: high for explicit abstract claims only
sources.access_evidence: Publisher indexed abstract returned by web search.
supported_claims: Abstract explicitly names value, rareness, imitability and organization as VRIO dimensions.

sources.title: Looking inside for competitive advantage
sources.author: Jay B. Barney
sources.reliability: high for explicit abstract claims only
sources.notes: Full text not inspected. Search-indexed author-hosted PDF redirected to an unrelated inaccessible domain on direct open; excluded as authority.
sources.access_evidence: Publisher abstract retrieved with title, author, date and DOI.
supported_claims: Article examines internal strengths and weaknesses and their competitive implications.
Environmental analysis needs complementary internal analysis.
